S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder is characterized by at least one lifetime manic episode, often accompanied by depressive episodes, with mood and energy changes that are clearly distinct from the person's usual functioning and cause marked impairment or require hospitalization. Manic episodes typically involve persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased goal-directed activity or energy lasting at least one week, though episodes can last months if untreated. The course is usually recurrent, with episodes triggered or unmasked by stressors, sleep disruption, or substance use, but not solely caused by them. It is distinguished from Bipolar II by the presence of full mania (rather than hypomania) and from unipolar depression or primary psychotic disorders by the cyclical pattern of mood elevation and depression and the temporal relationship between mood and psychotic features when present.

patient.stressor: Alfred’s first clear manic episode emerged over the seven months after he took on a demanding new role: studying nights for his Master Electrician exam while working overtime on a large commercial solar and home-automation contract. Initially, his family appreciated his extra drive and long hours in the garage planning a future family-run business, but as the project grew, he began insisting on expanding the scope, volunteering his small crew for unpaid extras, and pushing unsafe timelines that alarmed his supervisor. At home, his wife noticed that he stopped coming to Sunday barbecues and softball because he was constantly starting new side jobs and DIY electronics projects he refused to abandon, and their finances became strained when he unilaterally ordered expensive tools and solar inventory on credit for a business that didn’t yet exist. The breaking point came when a major customer complained about chaotic scheduling and Alfred’s increasingly confrontational, "wired" demeanor on-site, prompting his employer to pull him from field work; his wife, worried about his drastic change and inability to slow down or sleep, brought him to a psychiatrist after his apprenticeship mentees reported being scared by his intensity.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t seem to slow down—I’m constantly taking on new projects and working nonstop, like I’m stuck in overdrive.”

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Lately I swing from feeling on top of the world and like everyone should just get on my level, to snapping at my wife or my crew over the smallest thing, like someone misplacing a screwdriver, and once I start yelling I feel almost justified, like they’re the ones slowing down my big plans.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: It’s like my body and brain are stuck in high gear—after my shift I’ll hit the books for the Master Electrician test, then head to the garage to sketch out new business ideas and start wiring some new gadget, and before I know it the sun’s coming up and I’ve got three half-finished projects going and I’m still looking for more to do.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I honestly feel like I’m meant to revolutionize how people use solar and smart homes around here, like I can see solutions other electricians just aren’t smart enough to understand, so I ignore my boss and my wife when they tell me to slow down because I’m sure they’ll thank me once they see how big this is.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: Most nights I only lie down for two or three hours, if that, and even then my mind is racing with wiring diagrams and business plans so I just get back up, make coffee, and keep working because I don’t feel tired at all, just wired and almost annoyed at the idea of wasting time sleeping.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: When I’m trying to focus on wiring a panel or studying, every little thing yanks my attention away—the hum of a light, a text buzz, a new idea popping in my head—and I’ll drop what I’m doing halfway through to check the noise, start a new Google search, or sketch another design, until everything around me is a mess of started jobs I can’t seem to finish.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Since this all ramped up, my boss pulled me off field work because clients were complaining and my crew didn’t feel safe with my decisions, and at home my wife is furious about the debts I’ve run up and says I’m never really present with the family anymore.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, this whole overdrive stretch has been building and then staying intense for about seven months, ever since I took on the big solar contract and started cramming for the Master Electrician exam at night.
